correctness.rationale: Exact coefficient arithmetic verifies \(\dot H=b+ax\) and \(\dot E=-y^2+b(x+y)+a(H+x^2/2)\). When \(a=0\) and \(b\ne0\), unbounded linear drift of \(H\) excludes bounded forward-complete orbits. At \(a=b=0\), each leaf \(H=h\) is exactly the damped potential equation \(\ddot x+\dot x=x^2/2-h\) with energy dissipation \(\dot E_h=-v^2\). Compact alpha- and omega-limit invariance gives zero, one, or two equilibria depending on the sign of \(h\). At \(h>0\), the hyperbolic saddle has two unstable branches; a strict potential barrier bounds the left branch, while the right branch cannot be bounded, establishing the unique complete nonconstant bounded heteroclinic. Integration of the potential drop proves the exact action \(\frac{2}{3}(2h)^{3/2}\). For compact invariant probability measures the stationary energy identity forces support on the equilibrium line. All claimed parameter and limit cases have been checked analytically.

value.rationale: The zero-restoring plane is a natural parameter boundary of a standard quadratic chaotic flow. The theorem settles the entire bounded complete orbit geometry on that plane rather than giving an arbitrary parameter slice or a lone mean identity: for nonzero forcing no compact recurrence survives, whereas at zero forcing exactly one dissipative separatrix per positive height connects the two equilibrium branches, with an exact parameter-dependent action. This provides a sharp qualitative and quantitative boundary against which numerical near-degenerate dynamics can be checked.
